surface_mechanism_description: The surface reactions involve the hydrolysis of iron tert-butoxide (tBuO)6Fe2 and the ozone combustion of ferrocene (Cp2Fe). The hydrolysis reaction produces Fe2O3, while the combustion reaction also produces Fe2O3. These reactions are used to deposit Fe2O3 on porous alumina templates through atomic layer deposition (ALD). The reduction of Fe2O3 to Fe3O4 is achieved by treatment under 5% H2/95% Ar at 400 °C for 12 h.
evidence: We found6 that thin films of Fe2O3 can be obtained in ALD mode from either the hydrolysis of iron tert-butoxide, (tBuO)6Fe2, or the ozone combustion of ferrocene, Cp2Fe, with similar results; they are smooth and very homogeneously thick. When the reactions are applied to a porous alumina template, tubes are obtained with conformal wall thickness (Fig. 1) up to aspect ratios of approximately 100 (if the hydrolysis is used) and 1000 (with the combustion). The outstanding ability of the procedure to tune the geometry of the tubes appears clearly in the top panel of Fig. 1—changes in wall thickness as subtle as 1 nm can be observed unambiguously by the naked eye, and the intensity of the brown color furnishes an indication of the homogeneity of the deposition over several cm2. After reduction in the brown (semiconducting) Fe2O3 to black (metallic and ferrimagnetic) Fe3O4 by H2,7 the tubes are poised for systematic investigations into the influence of shape anisotropy over their magnetic properties;
